newsitem.title: USA: US Stockpile cobalt sale court hearing on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: US Stockpile cobalt sale court hearing on Thursday.

text.p: The U.S. Court of Federal Claims is due to hear a request Thursday afternoon for a temporary restraining order on U.S. Stockpile's proposed sale of one million lbs of higher grade cobalt by sealed bid.

Last Friday, Stockpile said it had postponed the March 31 opening of bids for the sale until April 7 following a request for a temporary restraining order to stop the sale filed by Minor Metals Inc, also known as Metal Resources Group Ltd.
In order to allow the Justice Department an adequate amount of time to prepare a response, the Stockpile agreed to delay the opening.
A final decision would probably not be reached by the judge at Thursday's hearing, but the Stockpile intended to continue with its bid opening on April 7.
It appeared that Minor Metals was unhappy with the Stockpile regulation that does not allow "all or none" bidding for metal.
Minor Metals officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Stockpile prefers to keep its options open and be allowed to award only some of the items bid for by any individual company.
The current ruling is applied to most of the Stockpile's commodity sales and was enforced in the two previous cobalt sealed bid offers.
